sites.why: Rule 8. The single LiteLLM acompletion call in _route_acompletion; transport is the litellm Router (complete() L1323, complete_json() L1923) or the litellm module (check_llm_health L1199). Provider/model/api_base come from config.json or env (LLM_PROVIDER default 'openai', LLM_API_BASE default None, so the OpenAI default endpoint), and the key comes from LLM_API_KEY or the app's config.json. The model is chosen at runtime; the default gpt-5-nano-2025-08-07 is a listed dated equivalence of gpt-5-nano. The user can switch provider to anthropic/gemini/groq/ollama/openrouter/azure/openai_compatible at runtime. Caveat: POST /config/llm-test passes a key from the request body into this call for pre-save testing (single-operator unauthenticated app, so not treated as per-user).
Rule 8. Retry of the same acompletion (L465) with max_completion_tokens after a max_tokens 400. Same transport, config, key and model as L465.

Rule 4. Raw httpx streaming POST to https://api.openai.com/v1/responses (store=false, stream=true) with a bearer token from the user's 'Sign in with ChatGPT' OAuth session (chatgpt_auth.get_access_token), i.e. a per-user plan credential, not the operator's API key. The model slug comes from the signed-in account's /v1/models list. Without rule 4 it would be rule 7 (handoff: raw HTTP to api.openai.com).

Rule 2 (by analogy). Provider 'claude_cli' runs the local `claude -p` binary via asyncio.create_subprocess_exec; the request goes out through the user's signed-in Claude Code CLI, not through any SDK or HTTP call in this repo, so there is nothing to point at Router. Not a listed counting unit; included for exhaustiveness.
Test helper: litellm.acompletion through an AsyncOpenAI client with an httpx MockTransport against https://synthetic.invalid/v1; never reaches the network.
